problem_markdown: Increasing positive-integer sequences $f(1),f(2),\ldots$ and $g(1),g(2),\ldots$ partition the positive integers and satisfy $g(n)=f(f(n))+1$. Determine $f(240)$.
solutions_markdown:
We have $f(1)=1$, since $g(1)\ge2$. No two consecutive integers lie in the $g$ sequence: the predecessor of $g(n)$ is $f(f(n))$.

If $f(n)=k$, count the integers up to $g(n)=f(k)+1$. Exactly $k$ belong to the $f$ sequence and exactly $n$ to the $g$ sequence. Hence $f(k)=n+k-1$. The next integer after $g(n)$ belongs to the $f$ sequence, giving $f(k+1)=n+k+1$.

Starting with $f(1)=1$, these two rules successively give
$$f(2)=3,\ f(3)=4,\ f(4)=6,\ f(6)=9,\ f(9)=14,$$
$$f(14)=22,\ f(22)=35,\ f(35)=56,\ f(56)=90,$$
$$f(91)=147,\ f(148)=239,\ f(240)=388.$$
Thus the required value is $388$.
